chunk_findings.detail: `problems` is documented as validating the fact record `{v, s, src, d, ver?, note?}` where only `ver` and `note` are optional, but it never checks the required `v` field. For example, `problems("facts.example", {"s": "verified", "src": "tool", "d": "2024-01-01"})` returns `[]`, so an incomplete fact with no value is treated as defect-free. Downstream code that assumes a fact has a value can then fail or treat the missing value as valid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/facts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: `_present` uses truthiness to decide whether a descriptor field is present, so legitimate falsey values (`False`, `0`, `""`, `[]`, `{}`) are silently omitted. For example, a section field `env = {}` is a descriptor value, but line 59 evaluates `(v := getattr(sec, sf.name))` as false and does not add `section.env` to the result. `rows` then produces no row for that fact, and `validate` (line 91) can reject an explicit overlay such as `[facts."section.env"] s = "verified"` with “status verified needs a value” even though the descriptor does have the value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (line 59)

chunk_findings.detail: For reserved sections, `none = true` does not suppress the section’s values. If `h.reserved["x"].none` is true but `h.reserved["x"].values` is `{"a": "1"}`, `_present` emits both `x: ("none", True)` and `x.a: ("1", False)`. `rows` then shows a value under a section documented as absent, and `validate` will accept an overlay for `x.a` with a readable status because the value is present. This contradicts the documented “section says none = true reads as status none” behavior and differs from the normal-section path, which `continue`s after seeing `none`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (lines 62-65)

chunk_findings.detail: `table` only replaces `|` in the `value` cell. Other interpolated fields, especially `source` from an overlay `src`, are not sanitized. Given an overlay entry with `src = "a|b"`, the generated markdown row contains an extra pipe and becomes an eight-column row under a seven-column header, corrupting the rendered facts table.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:table (line 126)

chunk_findings.detail: The `id="opencode"` filter assertion does not verify that any rows are actually returned. It only checks `all(r["agent"] == "opencode" for r in out.data["facts"])`, and `all()` is true for an empty iterable. If `harness_view` returns `exit=0`, a message containing `"opencode"`, but an empty `facts` list (for example because the filter compares the wrong field or accidentally drops all rows), this test still passes. Thus the id filter can be broken and the test will not catch it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_facts.py:test_view_facts_table_filters

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` validates `s`, `src`, `d`, and `ver`, but it does not require the documented required `v` field. For example, `problems("fact", {"s": "verified", "src": "x", "d": "2024-01-01"})` returns an empty list, so a verified fact with no value is accepted as defect-free. The module's own schema (`{v, s, src, d, ver?, note?}`) marks `v` as required; callers that trust `problems(...) == []` will store or render a fact with no value, and code that indexes `fact["v"]` will raise `KeyError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/facts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: `_present` decides whether a section field is a fact by truthiness (`if ... (v := getattr(sec, sf.name))`), and `validate` repeats the same mistake with `not value`. A descriptor field whose legitimate value is false-y (`False`, `0`, etc.) is therefore omitted from the fact set. For example, if a present section has `enabled = false` (or `timeout = 0`), `rows()` will not emit `section.enabled` at all; if the descriptor also has `[facts."section.enabled"] s = "verified"`, `validate` fetches `present.get(key, (None, False))` and raises `status verified needs a value` even though the descriptor explicitly supplies a value. This makes false/0 facts impossible to represent or validate, while reserved values are not filtered this way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` now rejects a readable status only when `is_none` is true; the previous `not value` guard was removed entirely. That means a known overlay key that `_present` omits because the underlying value is absent/`None` (not merely a falsey value such as `0`) now passes validation, and `rows` subsequently turns the missing value into `""`. For example, an overlay `[facts."section.field"] s = "verified"` for a known fact whose value is `None` or cannot be retrieved by the new attribute lookup validates successfully and renders a row with `status = "verified"` and an empty value. This is wrong because `verified`/`documented` should still require an actual value; the waiver should be limited to real falsey descriptor values, not to absence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:94

chunk_findings.detail: The new overlay-named falsey loop assumes that any dotted key in `h.facts` missing from `_present` is a falsey descriptor value, and re-reads the raw attribute directly. But `_present` also omits values when a section says `none = true`. Given a section such as `[sec] none = true` with `field = 1`, and an overlay `[facts."sec.field"] s = "verified"`, `_present` suppresses `sec.field`; `validate` now passes because it no longer requires a value and the subfact key is not itself the `none` marker; `rows` then executes `getattr(h.sec, "field")`, obtains `1`, and emits a verified row under a section documented as absent. This bypasses the `none = true` semantics and can reintroduce false “verified” facts under sections that should have no values.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:114

chunk_findings.detail: The new `given` handling is only applied to the normal-section loop; reserved sections are still emitted by the unchanged `for name, res in h.reserved.items()` loop, and `given_keys` cannot produce the keys reserved facts need. `given_keys` walks only one level of `raw.items()`, so a nested `[reserved.x] count = 0` either is skipped if `reserved` is in `_NOT_SECTIONS` or yields `reserved.x`, never `x.count`. As a result, an explicitly written falsey reserved value such as `[reserved.x] count = 0` is not added by `_present`; the `rows` overlay fallback also cannot rescue it because it looks up the section with `getattr(h, sec, None)`, while reserved sections live in `h.reserved`. Thus `ddflow harness facts` omits a fact the descriptor file explicitly wrote, and an overlay `[facts."x.count"] s = "verified"` is treated as naming no such fact, contradicting the new documented rule that a file-written key is a fact even when its value is `0` or `false`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (reserved-section loop)

chunk_findings.detail: `given_keys(raw)` is called after `raw.pop("mcp", None)` and `raw.pop("verified", None)`, so `Harness.given` cannot contain dotted keys from the `mcp` or `verified` sections. The new falsey-value behavior relies on `given` to know that a falsey descriptor value was explicitly written; values under sections that were popped before `given_keys` are therefore still treated as absent. For example, a descriptor that explicitly writes an empty MCP environment such as `[mcp] env = {}` (or another falsey `Mcp`/`Verified` field such as an empty `args` list) will not have `mcp.env` in `h.given`; `_present` then omits that fact, and an overlay naming it, e.g. `[facts."mcp.env"] s = "verified"`, can be rejected as naming a fact with no value even though the file explicitly wrote the value. This leaves the falsey-value fix incomplete for `mcp` and `verified` despite the new field’s comment saying it holds every key the file wrote.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:329

data.probe: mcp and verified are provenance of the file itself, excluded from the facts table by _NOT_SECTIONS; reserved values are strings only (parse_reserved)
data.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:329

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` is documented as validating the fact record `{v, s, src, d, ver?, note?}` where only `ver` and `note` are optional, but it never checks the required `v` field. For example, `problems("facts.example", {"s": "verified", "src": "tool", "d": "2024-01-01"})` returns `[]`, so an incomplete fact with no value is treated as defect-free. Downstream code that assumes a fact has a value can then fail or treat the missing value as valid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/facts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: `_present` uses truthiness to decide whether a descriptor field is present, so legitimate falsey values (`False`, `0`, `""`, `[]`, `{}`) are silently omitted. For example, a section field `env = {}` is a descriptor value, but line 59 evaluates `(v := getattr(sec, sf.name))` as false and does not add `section.env` to the result. `rows` then produces no row for that fact, and `validate` (line 91) can reject an explicit overlay such as `[facts."section.env"] s = "verified"` with “status verified needs a value” even though the descriptor does have the value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (line 59)

chunk_findings.detail: For reserved sections, `none = true` does not suppress the section’s values. If `h.reserved["x"].none` is true but `h.reserved["x"].values` is `{"a": "1"}`, `_present` emits both `x: ("none", True)` and `x.a: ("1", False)`. `rows` then shows a value under a section documented as absent, and `validate` will accept an overlay for `x.a` with a readable status because the value is present. This contradicts the documented “section says none = true reads as status none” behavior and differs from the normal-section path, which `continue`s after seeing `none`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (lines 62-65)

chunk_findings.detail: `table` only replaces `|` in the `value` cell. Other interpolated fields, especially `source` from an overlay `src`, are not sanitized. Given an overlay entry with `src = "a|b"`, the generated markdown row contains an extra pipe and becomes an eight-column row under a seven-column header, corrupting the rendered facts table.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:table (line 126)

chunk_findings.detail: The `id="opencode"` filter assertion does not verify that any rows are actually returned. It only checks `all(r["agent"] == "opencode" for r in out.data["facts"])`, and `all()` is true for an empty iterable. If `harness_view` returns `exit=0`, a message containing `"opencode"`, but an empty `facts` list (for example because the filter compares the wrong field or accidentally drops all rows), this test still passes. Thus the id filter can be broken and the test will not catch it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_facts.py:test_view_facts_table_filters

chunk_findings.detail: The falsey-value omission is still present; the diff only documents it as a limitation. `_present` still adds a descriptor field only when its value is truthy, so a legitimate falsey descriptor value such as `count = 0`, `enabled = false`, `env = {}`, or `tags = []` is treated as absent. For example, with `count = 0`, `_present` omits `section.count`, `rows` emits no row for that fact, and `validate` can reject an explicit overlay `[facts."section.count"] s = "verified"` because the fact is not considered present. The new docstring (“A falsy value … reads as not given”) records the behavior but does not make falsey facts representable, so valid facts with falsey values still cannot be recorded or verified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` now rejects a readable status only when `is_none` is true; the previous `not value` guard was removed entirely. That means a known overlay key that `_present` omits because the underlying value is absent/`None` (not merely a falsey value such as `0`) now passes validation, and `rows` subsequently turns the missing value into `""`. For example, an overlay `[facts."section.field"] s = "verified"` for a known fact whose value is `None` or cannot be retrieved by the new attribute lookup validates successfully and renders a row with `status = "verified"` and an empty value. This is wrong because `verified`/`documented` should still require an actual value; the waiver should be limited to real falsey descriptor values, not to absence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:94

chunk_findings.detail: The new overlay-named falsey loop assumes that any dotted key in `h.facts` missing from `_present` is a falsey descriptor value, and re-reads the raw attribute directly. But `_present` also omits values when a section says `none = true`. Given a section such as `[sec] none = true` with `field = 1`, and an overlay `[facts."sec.field"] s = "verified"`, `_present` suppresses `sec.field`; `validate` now passes because it no longer requires a value and the subfact key is not itself the `none` marker; `rows` then executes `getattr(h.sec, "field")`, obtains `1`, and emits a verified row under a section documented as absent. This bypasses the `none = true` semantics and can reintroduce false “verified” facts under sections that should have no values.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:114

chunk_findings.detail: The new `given` handling is only applied to the normal-section loop; reserved sections are still emitted by the unchanged `for name, res in h.reserved.items()` loop, and `given_keys` cannot produce the keys reserved facts need. `given_keys` walks only one level of `raw.items()`, so a nested `[reserved.x] count = 0` either is skipped if `reserved` is in `_NOT_SECTIONS` or yields `reserved.x`, never `x.count`. As a result, an explicitly written falsey reserved value such as `[reserved.x] count = 0` is not added by `_present`; the `rows` overlay fallback also cannot rescue it because it looks up the section with `getattr(h, sec, None)`, while reserved sections live in `h.reserved`. Thus `ddflow harness facts` omits a fact the descriptor file explicitly wrote, and an overlay `[facts."x.count"] s = "verified"` is treated as naming no such fact, contradicting the new documented rule that a file-written key is a fact even when its value is `0` or `false`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (reserved-section loop)

chunk_findings.detail: `given_keys(raw)` is called after `raw.pop("mcp", None)` and `raw.pop("verified", None)`, so `Harness.given` cannot contain dotted keys from the `mcp` or `verified` sections. The new falsey-value behavior relies on `given` to know that a falsey descriptor value was explicitly written; values under sections that were popped before `given_keys` are therefore still treated as absent. For example, a descriptor that explicitly writes an empty MCP environment such as `[mcp] env = {}` (or another falsey `Mcp`/`Verified` field such as an empty `args` list) will not have `mcp.env` in `h.given`; `_present` then omits that fact, and an overlay naming it, e.g. `[facts."mcp.env"] s = "verified"`, can be rejected as naming a fact with no value even though the file explicitly wrote the value. This leaves the falsey-value fix incomplete for `mcp` and `verified` despite the new field’s comment saying it holds every key the file wrote.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:329

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` validates `s`, `src`, `d`, and `ver`, but it does not require the documented required `v` field. For example, `problems("fact", {"s": "verified", "src": "x", "d": "2024-01-01"})` returns an empty list, so a verified fact with no value is accepted as defect-free. The module's own schema (`{v, s, src, d, ver?, note?}`) marks `v` as required; callers that trust `problems(...) == []` will store or render a fact with no value, and code that indexes `fact["v"]` will raise `KeyError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/facts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: `_present` decides whether a section field is a fact by truthiness (`if ... (v := getattr(sec, sf.name))`), and `validate` repeats the same mistake with `not value`. A descriptor field whose legitimate value is false-y (`False`, `0`, etc.) is therefore omitted from the fact set. For example, if a present section has `enabled = false` (or `timeout = 0`), `rows()` will not emit `section.enabled` at all; if the descriptor also has `[facts."section.enabled"] s = "verified"`, `validate` fetches `present.get(key, (None, False))` and raises `status verified needs a value` even though the descriptor explicitly supplies a value. This makes false/0 facts impossible to represent or validate, while reserved values are not filtered this way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the `not value` guard from the readable-status check, leaving only `is_none` as the rejection condition. For an overlay entry that names a schema field whose descriptor value is missing/None (for example, a present `[agent]` section that omits an optional `model` field, with `[facts."agent.model"]` containing `s = "verified"`), `_present` omits the field, `known` still contains it, and `present.get(key, (None, False))` yields `is_none=False`. `validate` then passes, while `rows()` later adds the key because it appears in `h.facts`, reads `None` via `getattr(..., name, None)`, stores `("", False)`, and the generated table renders `agent.model` as a verified fact with an empty value. The intended fix was to allow actual falsy values such as `False`, `0`, or `[]`, but the new condition also accepts “no value” facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: `rows()` now injects missing entries only for keys that appear in `h.facts` (`for key in h.facts: ... have[key] = ...`). The underlying `_present()` truthiness filter is not changed, so a descriptor fact whose value is false-y but has no provenance overlay is still absent from the generated table. For example, a descriptor containing `[caps]` and `subagent_depth = 0` but no `[facts."caps.subagent_depth"]` should produce a `caps.subagent_depth` row (value `0`, status `unverified`, visible with `--unverified`); the visible code produces no such row because `_present` omitted the falsy field and there is no `h.facts` key to trigger the new injection. This is the remaining half of previous finding #2: the change fixes overlay-named falsy values but not ordinary falsy descriptor facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new `given` logic is applied only to the loop over normal section fields. The following loop over `h.reserved` was not updated, so it still emits reserved-section fields only when their values are truthy. For a descriptor that writes an explicit false-y value in a reserved section, e.g. `[foo] bar = 0` where `foo` is collected in `h.reserved`, `given_keys` records `foo.bar`, but `_present` does not consult `h.given` in the reserved path and therefore omits `foo.bar` from the generated facts table. This contradicts the new docstring claim that “a key the file wrote (`given`) is a fact even when it is 0 or false” and means the explicit-zero fix is incomplete for reserved sections.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessfacts.py:_present (reserved-section loop)

data.summary: On HX-facts-core, rubber_duck/critic delta rounds re-sent the same documented limit (falsy value) under new digests across 4 rounds, so triaged 'confirmed/refuted' verdicts did not carry over and the budget (4 rounds, ~15 min each) was spent; gate only passed via 'passed on refutation' after round 4. Expected: a delta prompt that names the earlier verdict and probe per digest, or a verdict-carrying match on file+function.
data.title: ddflow review delta rounds re-raise an already triaged design point as a new finding

data.body:
Fixes bug B-review-delta-retriages-same-point: On HX-facts-core, rubber_duck/critic delta rounds re-sent the same documented limit (falsy value) under new digests across 4 rounds, so triaged 'confirmed/refuted' verdicts did not carry over and the budget (4 rounds, ~15 min each) was spent; gate only passed via 'passed on refutation' after round 4. Expected: a delta prompt that names the earlier verdict and probe per digest, or a verdict-carrying match on file+function. Found on HX-facts-core.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-review-delta-retriages-same-point --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-review-delta-retriages-same-point --regression-test <test>` first).
